title: Stress And Economic Health
gist: Didier Darcet (Gavekal-IS) uses a two-patient medical analogy to argue that resilience to shocks depends on pre-shock condition, and that the global economy today is in poor health — so the next shock could bring a slow, uncertain recovery (teaser only).

insights.claim: An economy's ability to withstand stress depends fundamentally on its condition before the shock, just as a healthy patient recovers quickly from an accident while a chronically ill one faces a long, uncertain recovery.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Assess vulnerability via starting conditions (debt, growth, buffers) rather than shock size when sizing downside scenarios.
insights.quote: In economics, as in medicine, the ability to withstand stress depends fundamentally on the condition of the system before the shock occurs.

insights.claim: Gavekal-IS argues the global economy today is in poor health, implying that a comparable external shock would produce a slower and more uncertain recovery than in a healthier starting position.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Bias toward defensive positioning and fatter left tails — recoveries from the next shock may be prolonged.
insights.quote: the global economy today is in poor health
insights.locator: And, as we argue in this letter
